tb21_profile.skill: Parse a modal, stateful machine-control instruction stream, reconstruct the 2D extrusion geometry it describes, render it, and read the glyphs back as a string
tb21_profile.domain: G-code / 3D printing (PrusaSlicer output for a Prusa MK4s), coordinate geometry, rasterising a toolpath into something visually readable
tb21_profile.task_form: analyse-and-report: determine what an artifact will do when executed, without the machine, and write the answer to a file

TMax-15K.reason: Requires real G-code semantics: modal Z state carried across lines, G1-with-E means extrusion, strip semicolon comments - the exact parse this task needs.
Extracts the X/Y of every G1 move into a coordinate stream: literally step one of reconstructing what the toolpath draws.
Parse G-code robustly across spacing variants and comments and reason about X/Y/Z coordinate values against bounds; same coordinate extraction problem.
Filter to G0/G1 lines, parse X and Y floats, apply offsets and re-emit; teaches the move-line grammar and coordinate-frame shifting.
Write an emulator for a DSL to determine what it would produce without executing it: the same predict-the-outcome-of-an-instruction-stream genre.
Accumulates E values across G1 lines - correct handling of extrusion parameters - but wrapped in archive-safety busywork.
Normalises G-code against rules that must first be read out of a PNG: combines the G-code grammar with pulling an answer out of a visual artifact.
Track a moving dot across frames to recover its trajectory coordinates: the inverse mapping between a picture and the path that made it.
Pulls the human-readable content out of G-code files (comment lines, odd encoding); same file family, but no geometry reasoning.
Extract frames and read the text rendered in them, then reconstruct the value: the read-glyphs-from-a-rendering half of this task.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Decode fixed-width binary lines into characters via a configured offset and print the recovered message; same decode-a-stream-into-text deliverable.
Recover a hidden message from an encoding spec and write it to result.txt: identical output shape, the whole answer is the decoded string.
Drives a tool that renders digit images as ASCII art and compares them; practice at making pixel data legible in a terminal.
Chain of steganographic extraction and decoding from images down to a final string; multi-step recover-the-text-from-an-artifact work.
Renders phrases as banner glyphs from a custom .flf font file: the forward direction of text-to-glyph-geometry, not the reading direction.
Whitespace-steganography decode where the two-symbol mapping must be inferred before the message reads out.
Same whitespace decode with a JSON report; repetitive family, kept for the decode-then-report shape.
Computes a distribution and renders it as a log-log PNG plot; the plot-it-to-see-it step, without needing to read anything back.
Pick the right payload from a manifest and decode it through a tool chain to recover content; decode-to-answer, no geometry.
Captures ASCII-art renderings of images plus predictions; weak, included because the corpus has no G-code or geometry content at all.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Downsample an image onto a coarse terminal cell grid so the picture is still recognisable: exactly how you make a toolpath readable in a terminal.
Renders data as an ASCII-art plot via gnuplot's dumb terminal; the plot-it-as-text trick this task's solution needs.
Emulate a binary's execution to recover its control flow rather than running it natively; simulating an instruction stream to learn its effect.
Work out the exact bytes a system would produce for a given submission and write them out: predict-the-output-and-report, byte-exact.
Decode a message hidden in a two-symbol encoding and report it; same shape of deliverable as 'what will the text show'.
Renders each N-Queens solution as a full N x N character board: turning coordinate data into a legible grid.
Encodes text into a QR pattern displayed as terminal blocks; exercises the text/visual encoding duality in the forward direction.
Turns a series of counts into a sparkline glyph row; small dose of data-to-visual-character mapping.
Multi-stage extraction of hidden content out of JPEGs until a readable string falls out; recover-the-text work in a different medium.
Extract just the human-readable body text out of a markup file; weakest kind of match, format-to-plain-text only.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Layout-mode text extraction places glyphs onto a character grid by coordinate; reconstructing readable text from positioned marks is this task's core.
cluster_list groups coordinates within a tolerance into rows - the same step needed to group extrusion segments into lines of letters.
ASCII rendering of a module grid fails with an index error; fixing it means getting the grid-to-character rasterisation right.
obj_to_edges converts positioned objects into geometric edges; same conversion from drawing primitives to structure.
A flip transform mirrors the wrong axis; catching an axis/orientation error is exactly the failure that makes rendered text unreadable.
SVG path output renders wrongly; debugging path-command emission is close kin to reading movement commands back into shapes.
Table extraction needs rows and columns inferred from line geometry; structure-from-coordinates reasoning.
CCITT decoding produces wrong bit patterns and cursor positions; raster reconstruction where an off-by-one ruins the image.
Slicing misbehaves with fractional coordinates; minor float-coordinate rounding discipline, which G-code parsing also needs.
Terminal monitor draws content at wrong positions; debugging a character-cell layout, the weakest of these but still spatial.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Writing points ignores scale and offset, silently moving every coordinate; the same scaled-integer-to-real-position arithmetic G-code needs.
change_scaling mutates x/y/z unexpectedly when merging files with different offsets; reasoning about coordinate frames across a machine data format.
Top-level assembly location is dropped, so geometry lands in the wrong place; transform composition in the CAD stack feeding 3D printing.
Scaling behaviour changed between versions, shifting point values; requires checking coordinate arithmetic against a reference.
Text is emitted twice into the rendered PDF with RTL runs; debugging glyph placement in generated drawing output.
Polylabel mishandles holes; a pure 2D computational-geometry fix, the kind of reasoning used to turn paths into regions.
STEP export deduplicates colours wrongly; same CAD/manufacturing file-format territory, little geometric reasoning.
A binary-template interpreter builds implicit arrays differently from the reference tool; interpret-a-format-per-spec skill.
Hyphenation breaks a word incorrectly during layout; fine-grained reasoning about where glyphs are placed on a line.
Layer visibility toggling corrupts the composited image; raster compositing correctness, adjacent to rendering a readable picture.

final_top10.reason: Real G-code semantics: modal Z state across lines, G1-with-E as extrusion, comment stripping - the parse this task's first half is.
Extracts X/Y from every G1 move into a coordinate stream: step one of reconstructing the drawn toolpath.
Filters to G0/G1 moves, parses X and Y floats and shifts them by an offset; the move-line grammar plus coordinate-frame handling.
Robust G-code coordinate parsing across spacing variants and comments, then reasoning about the values themselves.
Emulate an instruction DSL to report what it would produce without executing it: the same predict-the-outcome genre.
Rasterise an image onto a coarse terminal grid that still reads correctly: how you make a reconstructed toolpath legible.
Scale and offset silently ignored when writing points, moving every coordinate; the same scaled-coordinate arithmetic discipline.
Layout text extraction places glyphs on a character grid by coordinate: recovering readable text from positioned marks.
G-code normalisation whose rules must first be read out of a PNG; pairs the G-code grammar with reading an answer off an image.
Decode a fixed-width symbol stream into characters and print the recovered message; identical decode-a-stream-into-text deliverable.

notes: G-code exists only in TMax: a regex for gcode|toolpath|extruder|prusa|marlin matches 92 docs, all TMax-15K, zero in the other four corpora. So RTS/TW/Smith/Rebench are scored purely on the two component skills (parse-and-simulate an instruction stream; render geometry into something you can read back). The TMax shortlist itself is dominated by a false-positive family: ~60 near-identical 'organise this messy 3D-printing dataset / zip-slip archive' chores that merely mention .gcode and never parse a move line - I demoted all of them and promoted the four that actually parse G0/G1/E/Z. The TerminalWorld shortlist was the worst of the five (tw_12117 is literally 'write this text to /app/result.txt'); every TW entry above came from my own searches. RTS is weak here and its figlet ASCII-art family (dozens of near-duplicates) is the forward direction of glyph rendering, not reading, so I kept only one.
